title: feat: add MiniCPM4.1 SparDA host-resident prefetch
body_opening:
## Motivation

SparDA is a lookahead sparse-attention runtime. A Forecast projection at layer `l` predicts the KV blocks that layer `l+1` will need, so the runtime can stage them before the next attention call. This PR brings that path to MiniCPM4.1 and keeps it opt-in.

## Modifications

- Add the MiniCPM4.1 Forecast projection and checkpoint validation, including GQA/KV-head layouts and tensor parallel loading.
- Carry the per-request, per-layer forecast through `ForwardBatch` and `RadixAttention`, with a current-query fallback for the first layer.
- Add the LMCache logical-page adapter and a one-layer asynchronous prefetch path. Requests are protected by request generation and layer ident

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fold Q fp8 quantization into QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass
body_opening:
## Purpose

Fold the per-tensor Q→fp8 quantization into the AITER fused QK-norm+RoPE+KVcache kernel, so `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` no longer emits a separate `scaled_quant` per attention layer on the fp8-attention path. The fused kernel already fp8-quantizes K/V into the cache but returned Q in bf16, so the pass re-quantized Q separately (`_quantize_query` → `rocm_aiter_per_tensor_quant`). With the kernel emitting fp8 Q directly (ROCm/aiter#5914), the per-tensor path consumes it and drops that op.

Scope: RoPE + static per-tensor only. MRoPE and the per-head/group static-quant form keep the separate quantization.

**Stacked on #53918** (this edits the `quant_query` path #53918 introduces)

body_opening:
**FIX https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37319**

This PR adds INT8 per-token KV cache quantization to vLLM for the Triton attention backend.

Unlike the existing FP8 path, this mode uses dynamic per-token scales computed at cache-write time. In practice, this reduces KV cache memory roughly by half compared to bf16/fp16, offering a "plug and play" zero-config option without requiring pre-calibrated checkpoint scales.

This change introduces a shared INT8 KV cache contract for attention backends: dispatch via the `KVQuantMode` enum, declare auxiliary buffers through `AttentionSpec.auxiliary_buffer_specs`, allocate them upfront in the model runner, bind them via `AttentionImpl.

title: [Intel GPU] Add opt-in decode graph capture widths for DSV4 on XPU
body_opening:
## Motivation

The DSV4 indexer sizes its paged gather and its logits buffer from `MAX_SEQ_LEN_FOR_CAPTURE`, which is the **full configured context** — nothing about the request in hand. Graph capture freezes that width into the replayed graph, so at `--context-length 262144` a 128-token conversation performs full-context indexer work on every single decode step.

The width is read from the request-to-token pool, `deepseek_v4_backend.py`:

```python
self._full_seq_len_for_capture = self.req_to_token.shape[1]
```

At the launch configuration used below (`--context-length 262144 --page-size 256`) that is **262148**, not 262144 — the pool is padded. Every decode step paid for all of it.

title: [RadixTree] Reduce Stack Push/Pop Overhead for Leaf Nodes, Improve radix_tree Leaf Collection Performance
body_opening:
**Background**
Currently, when collecting leaf nodes, the process first traverses child nodes and pushes them onto the stack. Only after popping the nodes from the stack does it check if they are leaf nodes.

**Optimization**
During the traversal of child nodes, immediately check if a node is a leaf node:
If it is a leaf node, directly add it to the leaves collection.
Only push non-leaf nodes onto the stack.

**Benefits**
This optimization eliminates the unnecessary stack push and pop operations for all leaf nodes, reducing the associated overhead.
